title: Mexico’s Food for Well-Being Agency Expects Production of 10,000 Tons of Cacao in Tabasco
author: Alma E. Muñoz
content:
_This article by[Alma E.
Muñoz](https://www.jornada.com.mx/autores/Alma%20E.%20Mu%C3%B1oz,%20enviada)
originally appeared in the [September 25, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/09/25/politica/alimentacion-
para-el-bienestar-preve-produccion-de-10-mil-toneladas-de-cacao-en-tabasco),
Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Villahermosa, Tabasco**. In delivering a report on the progress of the
support programs for cacao producers, María Luisa Albores, director of
Alimentación para el Bienestar (Food for Well-Being), said that for the next
cycle **a production of 10,000 tons of cacao is expected in Tabasco** , of
which it is estimated that 1,000 tons will be collected.

At the presidential press conference held in this city, she commented that
currently most of the production is sold “en baba” (as fresh, unfermented
beans), which greatly reduces the sale price of their product, so it needs to
be fermented cacao, which, even though it takes a little longer, **raises the
price considerably**.

She explained that the federal government will invest **32 million pesos to
install 100 fermentation modules** in the ten cacao-producing municipalities
in the state, in order to facilitate this practice and so that producers earn
higher incomes from their production. Initially, these modules will make it
possible to process 6,000 tons of cacao, that is, **almost 60 percent of the
production**.
